interactions.summary: Jiang rejects the idea that God merely watches human behavior, and the class reframes the issue so that agency means people choose whether to turn toward God, who is always welcoming but never coercive.

Jiang names free choice as the fundamental law of the universe and asks why God would structure reality that way; one student says love and obedience must be willing, while another offers a speculative energy model Jiang has not yet endorsed.

claims.claim: Jiang says the correct framing is not that God watches people but that human beings choose whether to orient themselves toward God.
Jiang defines the universe's basic law as free choice: God is always welcoming, but every action still comes from a person's own will.
Jiang links this free-choice premise directly to Beatrice's later teaching in Paradise, presenting it as a governing interpretive principle for the book.
A student answer Jiang accepts says God gives free will so that love and obedience can be chosen rather than forced.

signature_moments.moment: Everything you do is your choice, even when you experience it as if it were not.
signature_moments.source_phrase: This is the fundamental law of the universe. It's all, everything is free choice.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the lecture's cleanest compression of Jiang's free-will cosmology and will matter repeatedly in later packets.

signature_moments.moment: God is always welcoming, but never coercing.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It keeps the balance between divine attraction and human agency that Jiang is building against both determinism and passivity.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's term for the fundamental law of the universe: God invites, but the movement toward or away from the light is entirely chosen.
A model in which salvation depends on the person's orientation toward a God who is already open rather than a judge surveilling behavior from outside.

chronology_notes.note: The discussion moves from correcting the spectator-God model to stating free choice as the lecture's governing cosmological law, which Jiang says Beatrice will later elaborate.

uncertainty_notes.note: The energy-accumulation answer is speculative student metaphor, not Jiang's settled cosmology, and should not be reused as a lecture claim.
